tests.title: A valid task form resolves the input, splits comma lists and collapses duplicate ids
given: a repo with a draft v2 package 09_agent_mode having tasks 1, 2, 3
then: exit code is 0
the change set and resolved ids contain 1 and 2 once each
the package was resolved as the report form resolves it
tests.pseudocode: parse(['09','--task','1,2','--task','2','--state','in_progress']); assert ids == [1,2]

tests.title: --task without --state and --state without --task are usage errors
given: a repo with a draft package
tests.when: speca 09 --task 1 and speca 09 --state done are each run
then: both exit 2
error stage is usage and category is usage
no result is carried
tasks.json is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: for argv in [['09','--task','1'],['09','--state','done']]: env=run(argv); assert env.exit==2 and env.error.stage=='usage' and env.result==nil

tests.title: A --state outside the four states is refused with the valid states as fix_hint
given: a repo with a draft package
then: exit 2, stage usage, category usage
fix_hint.flag is --state
fix_hint.valid is [pending, in_progress, done, dropped]
nothing is written
tests.pseudocode: env=run(['09','--task','1','--state','finished']); assert env.error.fix_hint == {flag:'--state', valid:[four]}

tests.title: Invalid --task values and next/all mixed with other values are usage errors
given: a repo with a draft package
tests.when: --task is given as 0, -1, abc, an empty item (1,,2), next,1, all,2, and next together with all
then: every call exits 2 at stage usage, category usage
nothing is written
tests.pseudocode: for v in ['0','-1','abc','1,,2','next,1','all,2','next,all']: assert run(['09','--task',v,'--state','done']).exit==2

tests.title: The task form combined with --validate or --list names two operations and is refused
given: a repo with a draft package
tests.when: speca 09 --task 1 --state in_progress --validate and speca --list --task 1 --state done are run
then: both exit 2 at stage usage, category usage
nothing is written
tests.pseudocode: assert run(['09','--task','1','--state','done','--validate']).exit==2

tests.title: No positional, two positionals, `-`, a URL or a multi-line input are usage errors in the task form
given: a repo with a draft package
tests.when: the task form is run with no input, with two inputs, with `-`, with https://example.com/x/issues/1, and with an input containing a newline
then: each exits 2 at stage usage, category usage
nothing is written
tests.pseudocode: for inp in [[],['a','b'],['-'],['https://example.com/x/issues/1'],['a\nb']]: assert run(inp+['--task','1','--state','done']).exit==2

tests.title: --force or --dry-run without --task is a usage error
given: a repo with a draft package
then: both exit 2 at stage usage, category usage
tests.pseudocode: assert run(['09','--force']).exit==2; assert run(['09','--dry-run']).exit==2

tests.title: A package that fails to load stops the task form as in the report form
given: a repo whose package 09 has malformed tasks.json
then: exit 1
error stage is load and category is input
no result is carried
tests.pseudocode: env=run(...); assert env.exit==1 and env.error.stage=='load' and env.error.category=='input' and env.result==nil

tests.title: Unknown task ids are refused, all named, with every plan id as fix_hint
given: a package with tasks 1, 2, 3
then: exit 2, stage usage, category usage
message names the package and ids 7 and 9
fix_hint is {flag: --task, valid: [1,2,3]}
tasks.json is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: env=run(...); assert '7' in msg and '9' in msg; assert fix_hint.valid==['1','2','3']

tests.title: An unknown id on a plan with no tasks says so and has no fix_hint
given: a package whose tasks array is empty
then: exit 2, stage usage, category usage
message says the plan has no tasks
fix_hint is absent
tests.pseudocode: env=run(...); assert env.exit==2 and env.error.fix_hint==nil

tests.title: --task next with no next task is refused with a reason matching the plan
given: plan A where every task is done or dropped
plan B where pending task 2 depends on task 1 that is dropped, and no task is in progress
tests.when: speca <spec> --task next --state in_progress is run on each
then: both exit 2 at stage usage, category usage
plan A message says every task is done or dropped and has no fix_hint
plan B message says no pending task has its dependencies done and fix_hint is {flag: --task, valid: [pending ids]}
tests.pseudocode: assert A.fix_hint==nil; assert B.fix_hint.valid==['2']

tests.title: --task all on a plan with no tasks is refused naming the package
given: a package whose tasks array is empty
then: exit 2, stage usage, category usage
message names the package
tests.pseudocode: env=run(['<spec>','--task','all','--state','done']); assert env.exit==2

tests.title: A package of format version other than 2 is refused with or without --force
given: a package whose schema_version is 1
tests.when: speca <spec> --task 1 --state in_progress is run, then again with --force
then: both exit 2 at stage usage, category usage
message says speca writes format version 2 only and a save would discard the v1 plan
all package files are byte-identical
tests.pseudocode: for extra in [[],['--force']]: assert run(base+extra).exit==2; assert bytes_unchanged()

tests.title: --task next resolves to the id NextTask returns, the report's next_task
given: a draft package with task 1 pending and task 2 pending depending on 1
then: exit 0
changes holds task 1 only
the report's next_task before the call was task 1
tests.pseudocode: assert report.next_task==1; env=run(next form); assert env.result.changes[0].id==1

tests.title: --task all skips tasks already in the target state and dropped tasks, in plan order
given: tasks 1 done, 2 in_progress, 3 dropped, 4 in_progress
target state is done
then: exit 0
changes are task 2 and task 4 in_progress → done, in plan order
tasks 1 (already done) and 3 (dropped) are not in changes
tests.pseudocode: run('all','done'); assert [c.id for c in changes]==[2,4]

tests.title: --task all resolving to nothing succeeds with no changes and writes nothing
given: every task is done or dropped
package files recorded byte-for-byte
then: exit 0
changes is empty
summary is `speca: <dir name> no task changed`
files and updated_at are byte-identical
tests.pseudocode: before=snapshot(dir); env=run(...); assert env.exit==0 and env.result.changes==[] and snapshot(dir)==before

tests.title: An explicit id already in the target state is judged by the machine and refused
given: task 1 is in_progress
then: exit 1, stage task, category lifecycle
tasks.json is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: env=run(...); assert env.exit==1 and env.error.stage=='task' and env.error.category=='lifecycle'

tests.title: Allowed moves of several tasks are checked together and applied in plan order
given: tasks 1 and 3 pending, 2 in_progress
then: exit 0
changes list task 1 then task 3 (plan order)
tasks.json holds both in_progress
tests.pseudocode: assert [c.id for c in changes]==[1,3]; assert disk states[1],[3]=='in_progress'

tests.title: A refused move refuses the whole call, names every refused task and carries the first refused task's targets
given: task 1 pending, task 2 in_progress, task 3 done
then: exit 1, stage task, category lifecycle
message names tasks 1 and 3 with current state and target, cites §8.3.1, and lists each one's allowed targets
fix_hint is {flag: --state, valid: [in_progress, dropped]}
tasks.json is unchanged, so task 2 stays in_progress
tests.pseudocode: assert fix_hint.valid==['in_progress','dropped']; assert disk_state(2)=='in_progress'

tests.title: A refused dropped task has no fix_hint and the message names --force as the way out
given: task 3 is dropped
then: exit 1, stage task, category lifecycle
fix_hint is absent
message says --force with done or pending is the only way out
tests.pseudocode: assert env.error.fix_hint==nil and '--force' in env.error.message

tests.title: A call applies every named move or none, never a subset
given: a temp package per generated plan
tests.when: for any plan of 1-8 tasks with arbitrary states and dependencies, any non-empty set of existing ids and any target state, with and without --force
then: either every named task not already skipped has changed to its target, or tasks.json is byte-identical to before
a refused call changes no task
tests.pseudocode: for plan,ids,target,force in gen(): before=snap(); env=run(); assert env.exit==0 or snap()==before; if env.exit==0: assert all(disk[i] in (target, before_state[i]) for i in ids) and all(disk[i]==target for i in changed)

tests.title: Sealed, superseded and archived packages are refused at stage status
given: three packages with status sealed, superseded, archived and a pending task each
tests.when: speca <spec> --task 1 --state in_progress is run on each
then: each exits 1, stage status, category lifecycle
no fix_hint
message says tasks can no longer change and a change is a new package that supersedes it
files are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: for st in [sealed,superseded,archived]: env=run(); assert env.error.stage=='status' and env.error.fix_hint==nil

tests.title: An active package with intent drift, or with a body lacking ## Intent, is refused at stage status before moves are checked
given: an active package whose PRD intent was edited after activation
an active package whose body lost its ## Intent while intent_hash is set
the call also names an unknown id
tests.when: speca <spec> --task 99 --state done is run on each
then: each exits 1, stage status, category lifecycle (not the usage error for the unknown id)
no fix_hint
message says the library refuses every write until the intent matches its hash again
tests.pseudocode: assert env.exit==1 and env.error.stage=='status'

tests.title: Status refusals are identical with --dry-run and with --force
given: a sealed package and an active package with intent drift
tests.when: the task form is run on each plain, with --dry-run and with --force
then: exit code, stage, category and message are the same in all three variants
files are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: base=run(a); for extra in ['--dry-run','--force']: assert same(base, run(a+[extra]))

tests.title: Save errors are mapped: *LifecycleError/*IntentError to status, *SaveError to write with its guidance
given: the save step is stubbed to return a *LifecycleError, an *IntentError, then a *SaveError
tests.when: the task form runs a change that would be written
then: lifecycle and intent errors give exit 1, stage status, category lifecycle
the save error gives exit 1, stage write, category disk, retryable false
write message says failure on temp files leaves the package unchanged, a failure during renames may leave some files updated, and to run `speca <spec>`
tests.pseudocode: stub.save=err; env=run(); assert (env.error.stage,env.error.category)==expected; assert env.retryable==false for SaveError

tests.title: Drafts and active packages without drift take task changes
given: a draft package
an active package whose intent matches its hash
tests.when: speca <spec> --task 1 --state in_progress is run on each
then: both exit 0
tasks.json holds task 1 in_progress in each
tests.pseudocode: for p in [draft, active]: assert run(p).exit==0 and disk_state(p,1)=='in_progress'

tests.title: --force makes refused moves to done or pending with the bypasses and allowed moves with the machine
given: task 1 pending, task 2 dropped, target pending, then task 3 pending and task 4 in_progress with target done
tests.when: speca <spec> --task 1,2 --state pending --force and speca <spec> --task 3,4 --state done --force are run
then: task 2 dropped → pending is made
task 4 in_progress → done is made as an ordinary move without forced flag
task 3 pending → done is made through the bypass
tasks.json holds the new states
tests.pseudocode: assert states after == expected; assert change(4).forced is absent

tests.title: Each bypassed task has a high task_state_forced warning and a forced change entry
given: tasks 2 and 3 are dropped, task 1 pending
then: warnings contain one task_state_forced per bypassed task (2 and 3), severity high, stage task, with from and to states
changes for tasks 2 and 3 carry forced true
task 1 has no warning
tests.pseudocode: assert count(w.code=='task_state_forced')==2 and all(w.severity=='high' and w.stage=='task')

tests.title: --force on a task already in the target state produces neither change nor warning
given: task 1 is done
then: exit 0
changes is empty
no task_state_forced warning
tests.pseudocode: assert env.result.changes==[] and no warning with that code

tests.title: --force does not bypass the machine for in_progress or dropped
given: task 1 is done and task 2 is dropped
tests.when: speca <spec> --task 1 --state in_progress --force and speca <spec> --task 2 --state dropped --force are run
then: both exit 1, stage task, category lifecycle
message says --force cannot set in_progress or dropped
tasks.json is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: assert 'cannot set in_progress or dropped' in msg

tests.title: --force skips no usage error, status refusal or legacy-version refusal
given: a draft package, a sealed package and a v1 package
tests.when: each is run with --force: an unknown id on the draft, a valid task on the sealed, a valid task on the v1
then: the draft call exits 2 at stage usage
the sealed call exits 1 at stage status
the v1 call exits 2 at stage usage
nothing is written in any
tests.pseudocode: assert exits == [2,1,2] and stages == ['usage','status','usage']

tests.title: Claiming a not-ready task goes ahead with a low task_not_ready warning naming the open dependencies
given: task 2 pending depends on task 1 which is pending
then: exit 0
task 2 is in_progress on disk
a warning task_not_ready, severity low, stage task, names task 2 and dependency 1
tests.pseudocode: w=find(warnings,'task_not_ready'); assert w.severity=='low' and '1' in w.message

tests.title: An invalid package still takes the change with one low spec_invalid warning naming the rules
given: a package with a dangling depends_on id and no unknown keys
then: exit 0 and the change is written
one spec_invalid warning, severity low, stage validate, naming the distinct Check (else Category) values
tests.pseudocode: assert count(spec_invalid)==1 and severity=='low' and stage=='validate'

tests.title: Unknown keys that the write would delete refuse the call at stage validate
given: tasks.json has an extra key `traceability` not allowed by the schema
then: exit 1, stage validate, category invalid_spec
no fix_hint
message lists the artifact and key
files are byte-identical
tests.pseudocode: assert env.error.stage=='validate' and 'tasks.json' in msg and 'traceability' in msg and snap==before

tests.title: --force writes over unknown keys with one high spec_invalid warning naming the removed keys
given: tasks.json has an extra unknown key
then: exit 0
the write happened and the key is gone from tasks.json
one spec_invalid warning, severity high, stage validate, naming the removed key
tests.pseudocode: assert warning.severity=='high' and key in warning.message and key not in read(tasks.json)

tests.title: A call raises at most one spec_invalid warning
given: packages generated with arbitrary validation failures, with or without unknown keys
tests.when: for any package and any valid task call, with and without --force
then: the warnings contain at most one with code spec_invalid
tests.pseudocode: for pkg,force in gen(): env=run(); assert count(w.code=='spec_invalid')<=1

tests.title: A change sets updated_at in UTC RFC 3339 and saves the package
given: a draft package with an old updated_at
then: tasks.json holds task 1 in_progress
prd.md frontmatter updated_at parses as RFC 3339 in UTC and is within the call's time window
tests.pseudocode: t0=now(); run(); ts=parse(frontmatter.updated_at); assert t0<=ts<=now() and ts.utc

tests.title: A success returns the full report on the written state plus changes in plan order
given: tasks 1 and 3 pending with no dependencies
then: exit 0
result carries every report-form field computed on the state written (task counts reflect the change)
changes are [{kind task, id 1, from pending, to in_progress}, {kind task, id 3, ...}]
tests.pseudocode: assert result.tasks.in_progress==2 and changes==[c1,c3]

tests.title: The summary names one change, several changes or none, with the dry-run suffix
given: a result with one change 2 pending → in_progress, one with changes 2 and 3 → done, and one with no changes
tests.when: the summary is built for the dir name 11_x, with and without dry run
then: `speca: 11_x task 2 pending → in_progress`
`speca: 11_x tasks 2, 3 → done`
`speca: 11_x no task changed`
each with ` (dry run, nothing written)` appended under --dry-run
tests.pseudocode: assert summary(...)==expected

tests.title: The summary always starts with the speca prefix and dir name and carries the dry-run suffix iff dry run
given: generated change lists
tests.when: for any list of 0-6 distinct task ids, any target state and any dry-run flag, the summary is built
then: it begins `speca: <dir name> `
it ends with ` (dry run, nothing written)` exactly when dry run is set
it contains `no task changed` exactly when the list is empty
tests.pseudocode: for ids,to,dry in gen(): s=summary(); assert s.startswith('speca: d ') and s.endswith(SUFFIX)==dry and ('no task changed' in s)==(ids==[])

tests.title: A refusal at status, task or validate returns the on-disk report with no changes and no next
given: a refused claim of an in_progress task
a sealed package
a package with unknown keys without --force
then: each exits 1
result is present with current task states
changes is absent and the envelope next is absent
tests.pseudocode: for env in refusals: assert env.result.tasks!=nil and env.result.changes==nil and env.next==nil

tests.title: --dry-run runs all checks and leaves the package byte-identical
given: a draft package with pending tasks
then: exit 0
every file in the package is byte-identical afterwards, updated_at included
tests.pseudocode: before=snap(); run(+'--dry-run'); assert snap()==before

tests.title: --dry-run returns the would-be result with dry_run true, changes and updated_at
given: a draft package with task 1 pending
then: exit 0
result.dry_run is true
result.changes is [{task 1 pending → in_progress}]
result.updated_at is the would-be new time, not the on-disk one
summary ends with ` (dry run, nothing written)`
tests.pseudocode: assert r.dry_run and r.changes[0].to=='in_progress' and r.updated_at != disk.updated_at

tests.title: --dry-run returns the same refusal as the real call
given: a refused claim (task in_progress), a sealed package, and an unknown-key package
tests.when: each is run with and without --dry-run
then: exit code, stage, category, message and fix_hint are the same in each pair
tests.pseudocode: for c in cases: assert same(run(c), run(c+['--dry-run']))

tests.title: A dry run suggests the same call without --dry-run, naming resolved ids and keeping --force
given: tasks 1 and 2 pending, no dependencies
tests.when: speca <spec> --task all --state in_progress --force --dry-run is run, and again on a plan with no changes
then: next has one entry {tool speca, input spec_dir, flags [--task, 1,2, --state, in_progress, --force]}
with no changes next is empty
tests.pseudocode: assert next==[{tool:'speca',flags:['--task','1,2','--state','in_progress','--force']}]

tests.title: The report form suggests the claim of a ready next_task on a writable package with nothing in progress
given: a draft package with task 1 pending and ready
an otherwise identical package with a task in_progress
a sealed package with a ready task
then: the first has next containing {tool speca, input spec_dir, flags [--task,1,--state,in_progress]}
the second and the sealed one do not contain a claim
tests.pseudocode: assert claim in next(a); assert claim not in next(b) and not in next(c)

tests.title: The list form suggests the claim for the first active package that is claimable
given: active package 05 with a task in_progress
active package 07 with intent drift
active package 08 with a ready pending task and no drift
active package 09 also claimable
then: next contains the claim of package 08's ready task and none for 09
tests.pseudocode: assert next==[claim('08', task)]

tests.title: After a move next is the report's next on the new state
given: task 1 pending then done-able, task 2 pending depends on 1
tests.when: task 1 is claimed, then task 1 is set done
then: after the claim next is `specr <spec_dir> --task 1`
after the done next is the claim of task 2
after the last task is done next is empty
tests.pseudocode: assert next1[0].tool=='specr'; assert next2==claim(2); assert next3==[]

tests.title: CategoryLifecycle is "lifecycle" and not retryable
given: the envelope package
tests.when: CategoryLifecycle and RetryableFor(CategoryLifecycle) are read, with RetryableFor of api and usage
then: CategoryLifecycle == "lifecycle"
RetryableFor(CategoryLifecycle) is false
existing categories keep their retryability
tests.pseudocode: assert CategoryLifecycle=='lifecycle' and !RetryableFor(CategoryLifecycle) and RetryableFor(CategoryAPI)

tests.title: The task warning codes have their values and stage task
given: internal/cli and envelope packages
tests.when: WarnStage is asked for the two codes and the aliases are compared with the envelope constants
then: WarnTaskNotReady == "task_not_ready" and WarnTaskStateForced == "task_state_forced"
WarnStage of each is "task"
the internal/cli aliases equal the envelope constants
tests.pseudocode: assert cli.WarnStage(cli.WarnTaskNotReady)=='task' and cli.WarnTaskStateForced==envelope.WarnTaskStateForced

tests.title: Change, changes and dry_run round-trip through DecodeSpeca and are omitted when empty
given: an AdminResult with two changes (one forced) and dry_run true, and one without either
tests.when: each is encoded to an envelope and decoded with DecodeSpeca
then: changes and dry_run round-trip equal
the second encodes neither a changes nor a dry_run key
a Change with kind task omits unset from/to/forced fields
tests.pseudocode: b=json(env); assert decode(b).changes==changes; assert 'changes' not in json(env2)

tests.title: speca --help describes the task form and its flags
given: the speca command
then: the help text mentions the task form, --task, --state, --force and --dry-run
tests.pseudocode: out=run(['--help']); for k in ['--task','--state','--force','--dry-run']: assert k in out

tests.title: speca --schema equals the regenerated golden file and describes the new flags, fields and exit codes
given: cmd/speca/testdata/schema.golden.json regenerated
then: output equals the golden file byte for byte
--state is an enum of the four states
flags --task, --force, --dry-run and result fields changes and dry_run are described
exit codes 1 and 2 mention refusals
tests.pseudocode: assert Main(['--schema','--dir','/nonexistent','anything']) == read(golden)

tests.title: An agent claims the next ready task through the report's suggestion, then finishes it
given: a copy of a draft v2 package with task 1 pending and ready, on disk under .specs/
tests.when: speca <spec> is run, then speca <spec> --task next --state in_progress, then speca <spec> --task 1 --state done
then: the report's next holds the claim for task 1
the claim exits 0 with changes [{task 1 pending → in_progress}] and next `specr <spec_dir> --task 1`
tasks.json holds task 1 in_progress, then done
updated_at is set after each write
the done call's next is the next ready task's claim or empty

tests.title: A second agent's claim of a taken task is refused with the allowed states and the on-disk report
given: a package with task 1 in_progress on disk
then: exit 1, stage task, category lifecycle
fix_hint is {flag: --state, valid: [pending, done]}
result carries the on-disk report without changes or next
tasks.json and prd.md are byte-identical

tests.title: A dry run of a forced recovery of a dropped task, then the suggested real call
given: a package with task 3 dropped on disk
tests.when: speca <spec> --task 3 --state pending --force --dry-run is run, then the suggested call from next is run
then: the dry run exits 0 with dry_run true, changes [{task 3 dropped → pending, forced true}], a high task_state_forced warning and files unchanged
next is `speca <spec_dir> --task 3 --state pending --force`
the real call writes the package so tasks.json holds task 3 pending
